mobile-system-design.md: Start with a repeatable design method and the non-functional requirements every design must meet, then the platform building blocks mobile systems share, then complete systems such as sync, feeds, payments and media. Follow the guided phases or open a chapter directly.
mobile-system-design/design-framework.md: A design interview rewards scope, one clear diagram and depth on one problem. Learn the method: how to pace the round, the 12-section template every walkthrough here uses, the mistakes that sink candidates and the libraries to default to.
mobile-system-design/non-functional-requ: Features demo well; qualities decide whether they survive production. Use this menu of 13 mobile NFRs to pick the few that change a design, turn each into a measurable budget, and name the trade-offs between them.
mobile-system-design/performance.md: Users feel jank, slow starts, drained batteries and wasted data long before they file a bug. Walk through the interview: per-tier budgets, the levers for rendering, memory, battery and network, and a deep dive on frame rate.
mobile-system-design/accessibility.md: Every screen must work with TalkBack, large text, high contrast, big touch targets and reduced motion. Learn the practices: Compose semantics, contrast tokens, captions, automated checks and the manual pass no tool replaces.
mobile-system-design/localization-and-in: An app shipping to 30 markets needs translations, plurals, locale formats and right-to-left layouts from day one. Learn the practices: string discipline, formatting, RTL, in-app language switching, the translation workflow and testing.
mobile-system-design/security-and-privac: Tokens, transport, stored data and personal data each need their own defence, and none of them is enough alone. Learn the practices: TLS, Keystore-backed storage, biometric gates, app integrity, runtime protections and privacy compliance.
mobile-system-design/versioning-and-back: Old app versions stay installed for months while the server and the database schema move on. Walk through the interview: additive API contracts, tested Room migrations, sunset runbooks, and a deep dive on force-update and soft deprecation.
mobile-system-design/offline-sync.md: Users edit notes without a network and expect nothing lost, nothing duplicated and nothing silently overwritten. Walk through the interview: requirements, an outbox-first architecture, safe retries and a conflict policy.
mobile-system-design/app-startup.md: Users judge an app by how fast it opens, and every SDK wants to start in Application.onCreate. Walk through the interview: TTID and TTFD budgets, the startup phases, measuring in the field and in CI, and a deep dive on deferred initialization and Baseline Profiles.
mobile-system-design/authentication.md: Sign-in has to stay secure, survive restarts and refresh silently on bad networks without bouncing the user. Walk through the interview: Authorization Code with PKCE in the browser, a Keystore-backed token vault, and a deep dive on the token lifecycle with single-flight refresh.
mobile-system-design/deep-links-and-univ: One URL should open the right screen on web, iOS and Android, even after an install or behind a login. Walk through the interview: verified App Links, deferred deep links, one router for every entry point, and a deep dive on routing and verification.
A notification must arrive when the app is backgrounded or killed, render richly and open the right screen. Walk through the interview: FCM token registration, data versus notification messages, channels, the Android 13 permission, and a deep dive on the receive pipeline.
mobile-system-design/feature-flags-and-r: Flags must read instantly, stay stable for a session and still work offline, while the server can change them at any time. Walk through the interview: typed flags, targeting, a last-good cache on disk, and a deep dive on evaluation and the fetch cycle.
mobile-system-design/telemetry-sdk.md: Crashes are rare and must never be lost; performance metrics are constant and can be sampled. Walk through the interview: JVM, native and ANR capture, frame and startup metrics, battery-conscious batching, and a deep dive on persisting a crash and delivering it.
mobile-system-design/analytics-sdk.md: Every feature tracks events without blocking, and once an event is queued it must survive a crash, a kill or a dead network. Walk through the interview: consent, identity, bounded storage, and a deep dive on the write, buffer and flush pipeline, including which failures retry and which events are dropped on purpose.
mobile-system-design/image-loading.md: One image request has to get through two cache tiers, a possible source fetch, a decoder and a list that keeps scrolling, without blocking the main thread or reaching the wrong row. Walk through the interview: cache keys by size and transformation, bounded bitmap memory, and a deep dive on the request pipeline, including cancellation and what each failure does.
mobile-system-design/file-downloader.md: A large download must survive dropped networks and a killed process without exposing a partial file, and resume without starting again when the server allows it. Walk through the interview: a durable queue, HTTP Range requests, bounded parallel chunks, and a deep dive on resuming from the ledger, including servers that ignore a range and files that change mid-download.
mobile-system-design/caching-library.md: A two-tier cache has to stay fast, bounded and safe from torn files, while being honest that it may lose an entry. Walk through the interview: eviction budgets, atomic disk writes, lazy expiry, and a deep dive on the read and write paths, including the races between them.
mobile-system-design/pagination.md: A long list needs pages from the network, a cache that works offline and a saved scroll position, though restoring a far position still needs a device test. Walk through the interview: cursors and remote keys, Room as the source of truth, and a deep dive on RemoteMediator, including what a failed page shows and what happens after process death.
mobile-system-design/typeahead-autocompl: Suggestions must feel immediate while the text keeps changing and the network may be slow or absent. Walk through the interview: debounce sizing, cancelling out-of-date queries, private local recents, and a deep dive on merging local and remote results, including why remote failures stay quiet.
mobile-system-design/search.md: A results screen has to keep one query, its filters and its cached pages consistent while the user changes their mind. Walk through the interview: server-side ranking and facets, a cache kept per account and query, and a deep dive on the query lifecycle, including what offline can and can’t show.
mobile-system-design/notification-system: Many notification failures are decisions, not transport: the wrong channel, the wrong language, a double send or a ping during quiet hours. Walk through the interview: triggers, preferences, frequency caps and a durable inbox, and a deep dive on routing, including what happens when a channel is down.
mobile-system-design/news-feed.md: A personalised feed has to scroll smoothly, open from its cache when the network is gone and show each account only its own posts. Walk through the interview: cursor paging through Room, bounded video and images, optimistic likes, and a deep dive on paging, scroll restoration and what a restart can and can’t bring back.
mobile-system-design/chat-messaging.md: An outgoing message has to be saved before the network is touched, and a retry must not deliver it twice. Walk through the interview: client-generated ids, Room as the single source of truth, the WebSocket lifecycle, FCM priority for a closed socket, and a deep dive on the send flow and where it can still fail.
mobile-system-design/collaborative-editi: Local edits must feel instant while other people change the same document, and an edit the user saw has to survive a crash, even offline. Walk through the interview: a CRDT SDK as a black box, an op log beside a debounced snapshot, ephemeral presence, and a deep dive on the order of apply, persist, show and send.
